I got kex-close on .9/.100 first and REFUSED on retry ~2 min later, which says something on that host is TRANSITIONING (booting? sshd flapping?), not statically off. ALWAYS RUN THE CONTROL. `ssh chi-srv-01` succeeded in the same minutes (returned hostname + 2026-07-30T21:18:26-05:00), which is what turns 'I cannot reach the Pi' from a claim about MY box into a claim about the PI. Two commands. Do it before routing any connectivity finding.

--- PRIOR (US-499, S6 render-regression backstop) ---

SPRINT 66 (V0.29.20) -- US-499 (S6 render-regression backstop) DONE, 5/7. REMAINING TWO (US-478, US-497) ARE BOTH BLOCKED BY BL-026 -- there is no dev work left in this sprint; the next move is CIO (wire the IMU, AI-005) + Atlas (rule on the states/imu contract Q-A/Q-B), not another iteration.
THE HEADLINE LESSON: TO CATCH A COMPOSITION BUG, SPLIT THE HARNESS ALONG THE SEAM THE BUG CROSSED. All three defects this sprint fixed had one shape -- every part tested green and the composition was broken (S1: a dependency the entry point never injected, computeBootState was always right; S2: correct JS defeated by a stylesheet the JS cannot see; S5: three valid CSS declarations interacting to a black screen). So the backstop is TWO PROCESSES THAT CANNOT SEE EACH OTHER'S VERDICT: node runs the SHIPPED carousel.js / boot-state-poll.js against a mini-DOM and dumps the attributes (it knows nothing about CSS); Python resolves the SHIPPED stylesheet over that DOM and answers the only question that matters -- does this element have a box. Neither half can launder the other's answer. That property is what every existing UI test lacked.
THE LOAD-BEARING DETAIL, and it generalises to any DOM harness: IDL properties must REFLECT to CONTENT ATTRIBUTES. `el.hidden = true` has to land as the `hidden` ATTRIBUTE, because the attribute is what the cascade selects on. A harness storing it as a private flag would have reproduced US-495's BLIND SPOT and passed the broken stylesheet without a murmur. Everything else in mini_dom.js is scoped to the ~15 DOM methods the kits actually touch -- enumerated from the source with grep, not guessed. It is not a jsdom clone and must not grow into one.
PROVEN RED AGAINST REAL HISTORY, not asserted: `git show <fixcommit>^:<path>` gives you the actual defective artifact, and a stdlib-only module can be loaded LIVE via importlib and run. The pre-US-495 stylesheet reproduces all six overlays painting at idle; the pre-US-494 emitter, wired the way its own entry point wired it (no obdProbeFn -- that OMISSION is the bug), pins the splash with the literal 'eclipse-obd: not ready (starting)'. Because history is not guaranteed (shallow clone / CI), TWO MUTATION proofs run unconditionally beside them (delete the [hidden] guard rule; strip just its !important). Pattern worth reusing: git artifact = the literal claim, mutation = the one that still runs everywhere.
THE TEST FOUND A BUG IN MY OWN HELPER, which is the best evidence it works: I built the emitter BEFORE installing the fake clock, so startMono was the REAL boot time and elapsed() was hugely negative -- no hard cap could ever fire. EVERY POSITIVE TEST STILL PASSED (healthy does not depend on elapsed); only the pre-fix RED test noticed, by reporting the generic fallback instead of the emitter's own message. That is this whole story in miniature. Also: restore a patched `time.monotonic` in a finally -- it is global, and the same process shells out to node moments later, under subprocess's own timeout bookkeeping.
CLOSED US-496's NAMED GAP: the page dots are JS-CREATED, so the static markup sweep (test_dashboard_overlay_hidden_guard.py) can never reach them. They are now built by the real carousel.js and rendered through the real cascade, asserted against the visible-card geometry BOTH ways -- bench (gated card + its dot absent) and vehicle-connected (both revealed). US-496 called the dot count 'the one thing the new geometry could get wrong in a way no unit test sees'.
FIDELITY LIMIT + THE MECHANISM THAT STOPS IT BEING SILENT: this resolves the CASCADE, not LAYOUT -- it sees 'not painted', never overflow/wrapping/off-screen; sibling combinators unresolved. A skipped `display` rule makes every test LENIENT (falsely green), which is the one failure mode a backstop must not have -- so unresolvableDisplaySelectors() REPORTS any display rule behind a pseudo-class it cannot evaluate and a test FAILS when one appears. Teach the resolver or move the rule; do not delete that test. Also added test_theRealJsActuallyRan: a harness that silently no-ops would make every 'nothing paints' assertion pass for the wrong reason.
GREEN (synchronous, in-loop): 15 new tests, 0 skipped (both git RED proofs ran for real); tests/ui + tests/pi/splash = 434 passed / 1 skipped; ruff clean. NO PRODUCTION CODE CHANGED -- test infrastructure + docs only, so nothing shipped to the Pi can have regressed. TD-068 handled in place (probe runner sets encoding='utf-8'; a render backstop must not introduce the fault class it exists to catch). ARCHITECTURE DoD met in-sprint: F-092 'Render-regression backstop' subsection + xrefs from the F-103 readiness contract and the US-495 surface invariant.
NO ON-PI GATE OWED FOR THIS STORY -- that is the point of it. But it does NOT retire the ones owed by US-494/495/496/498: it covers 'does this element have a box', the panel still owes 'does it look right and does the motion feel right'. Carried debt: TD-067, TD-068 (mitigated here, not closed), TD-069.

--- PRIOR (US-498, S5 closeout/shutdown splash) ---

THE HEADLINE LESSON: REVERSING AN ANIMATION IS TWO REVERSALS, AND SHIPPING ONE OF THEM IS A BLACK SCREEN. The kit flipped `animation-direction: reverse` on every class with a comment saying 'the keyframes are symmetric enough that reverse just works'. Direction was the easy half; the running ORDER also has to reverse. The boot timeline ENDS with a fadeout DELAYED 6s, and `animation-fill-mode: both` holds the reversed animation's FIRST RELEVANT keyframe through that delay -- which for direction:reverse is `to`, i.e. opacity 0. So the fill-mode that exists to prevent a flash of unstyled content pinned the mark invisible for 6 seconds of a 7-SECOND GRACE WINDOW (pi.powerWatch.smoothingSec): black for essentially the whole shutdown. Fix = reversed delay is T - (bootDelay + bootDuration), T = 6.5s; derived from splash.svg, no invented numbers, and the test RE-DERIVES them so re-timing the boot re-aims the closeout.
NOTE THE SHAPE OF THE BUG, because it will recur: three individually-correct declarations (a delay, a fill-mode, a direction) interacting. Every part had a passing test. Every surrounding component worked -- sequencer emitted, emitter wrote, .path watched the right file, server served the right page with the token, JS revealed the stage on time. The surface it revealed was black. When a UI 'does nothing' and all the parts test green, stop testing parts and start SAMPLING THE OUTPUT ON A CLOCK.
SO THAT IS WHAT THE TEST DOES: tests/ui/test_shutdown_splash_render.py resolves the shipped CSS (cascade + !important, comma-list shorthands, fill-mode/direction/delay) and samples the mark's opacity every 250ms across the real grace window read from config. RED naming every blank instant t=[1.0..6.0]. One assertion I wrote OVER-CLAIMED -- 'brightness never rises' failed on the DESIGNED throb, whose recovery genuinely raises brightness -- and I corrected the test to the honest envelope claim (max->low endpoints, second half never brighter than the first) rather than keeping a green-looking lie. Fidelity limit is stated in the file: easings treated as linear, so endpoints and the SIGN of a change are exact, mid-segment values are not; every assertion is zero-vs-nonzero or an endpoint.
A KEEP-LIST IS A COST, NOT A SAFETY NET -- the deploy half, and it generalises. US-495 keep-listed the closeout surface as 'the kit's install.sh owns those'. But a keep-listed asset is never installed, never pruned and never byte-verified; its only refresh path was the A-9 kiosk step, which is ALLOWED TO WARN AND SKIP (install.sh aborts if it cannot detect session type or chromium). So the stale hole US-495 closed for boot was still open for shutdown -- where it only shows itself DURING a shutdown, nobody watching, no re-run. Moved the whole surface into the manifest (both installers copy identical bytes from the same synced kit, so ownership costs nothing and buys the verify). Keep-list is now version.txt alone, which earns it: the deploy GENERATES it, so the manifest cannot name it. Ask of any keep-list entry: who verifies this, and are they allowed to skip?
WIRING PINS, green on arrival and labelled as such (contract pins, not a TDD claim): tests/pi/splash/test_shutdown_splash_wiring.py drives a REAL sequencer grace into a real states dir, serves the REAL kit over the REAL states_http, and fetches the page at the URL extracted FROM THE SHIPPED UNIT FILE -- nothing asserted against a literal a rename would leave behind on both sides. US-494's lesson one story later.
TD-069 FILED, READ IT BEFORE THE ON-PI CHECK: nothing ever REMOVES shutdown-state. /run is tmpfs, so a CANCELLED grace (the common case -- that is what smoothing is for) leaves phase:cancelled on disk for the rest of the uptime and PathExists has no false->true transition left: the SECOND grace of a boot gets NO closeout splash. I also SUSPECT but did NOT confirm a systemd re-trigger loop on the cancel path -- stated as unverified, not asserted. Root: the file has a write lifecycle and no clear lifecycle. Fix is producer-side (the power path that bricked the Pi once, I-038) -> Atlas decision, not a drive-by edit in a render story.
BL-026 FILED: US-478 + US-497 are DOUBLE-gated and I refused them rather than fake progress. (1) hardware -- no 0x69 on the bus (AI-005, CIO); (2) and the one that matters more, the states/imu SHAPE is still gated on Atlas Q-A (derived-field contract) + Q-B (higher-rate transport). Building a heading/grade/tilt-comp bridge to an unconfirmed contract with no hardware = inventing the numeric contract then testing against my own invention. US-499 (S6) is unblocked and is the highest-value story left: S1/S2/S3/S5 have EVERY ONE of them ended with an owed on-Pi render check, which is exactly the gap S6 closes.
GREEN (synchronous, in-loop): 745 passed / 2 skipped across tests/ui + tests/pi/splash + tests/deploy; ruff clean on all three touched .py; bash -n clean; ran the real --dry-run and read the splash step's own preview line (the deploy tests parse that same line). HOST GAPS unchanged: make/black/mypy absent on this Windows box. ARCHITECTURE DoD met in-sprint: F-103 gained a 'Closeout (shutdown) surface -- the reversal contract' subsection, and I CORRECTED the US-495 /opt asset-ownership table this change made wrong.
